executive_summary: The feature adds an internet-facing endpoint to NME that lets any Teams user in the customer tenant trigger a privileged ARM operation (VM restart) against a session host, using the NME managed identity. The security value is low data exposure (no new persisted data beyond audit entries) but high control-plane sensitivity: a flaw in how the caller is authenticated or how the user is mapped to a host turns a convenience feature into a way to disrupt other users' desktops. The policy engine places the feature at Tier 2 and enumerated 54 threats: 34 High and 20 Medium at default (conservative) scores, none Critical because the feature is single-tenant and no Restricted data is persisted. Most of the High scores come from the internet-facing entry point uplift and will fall once the team rescores with the planned controls in place. With strict JWT and tenant validation, object-id based host resolution, server-side rate limiting and a secure-by-default enable flag, the residual risk is manageable.
rating_rationale: Internet-reachable entry point, new authentication path and a privileged Azure operation on customer compute (ISMS-DEV-003 §6.2 'elevated security risk'). No cross-tenant or Restricted-data exposure keeps it below Critical.

domain_impacts.summary: New inbound trust in Bot Framework JWTs; issuer, audience, expiry and tenant must be validated on every activity (T-P1-FEAT-004, T-P1-S-001, T-P1-S-002).
Authorization is implicit in the user-to-host mapping; the managed identity holds VM Contributor on the resource group (T-P2-FEAT-001, T-P2-E-002).
A new public endpoint needs replay protection, size limits and rate limiting (T-P1-S-002, T-P1-D-001, T-F2-D-004).
Restarts must be attributable to the Teams user and the admin flag changes must be logged (T-P1-R-001, T-P2-R-001).
Entra object id and display name are processed transiently; only the audit entry is persisted. Message text should not be stored.
The per-host-pool flag is the primary control and must default to off (T-P2-FEAT-003).
Restart loops and ARM throttling affect the whole host pool (T-P1-FEAT-002, T-P1-D-001).
NME is single-tenant, but a multi-tenant bot registration would make tenant validation a hard requirement (open question).
Bot credentials used for outbound confirmation cards must live in Key Vault; the worker uses managed identity for ARM (T-P2-S-003).
Activity payloads cross the internet boundary; schema-validate and never echo message text into cards unescaped (T-F2-T-002).
Platform TLS and Microsoft-issued JWT signing; no new cryptographic design.
Bot Framework SDK must come from the Approved Tools List and pass SCA (T-P1-T-005).

key_risks.headline: Accepting a forged or foreign bot activity
key_risks.why_it_matters: The endpoint is reachable from the internet and its only guard is the Bot Framework JWT. If audience or tenant checks are missing, anyone who can obtain a Bot Framework token for another bot or tenant can restart hosts in this customer's environment.
required_controls: Validate JWT signature against Bot Framework OpenID metadata, issuer, audience = this bot's app id, and expiry on every request
Reject activities whose tenant id is not the NME customer tenant, regardless of bot registration type
Apply a 5-minute replay window using the activity id and timestamp

key_risks.headline: Restarting the wrong host, or more hosts than intended
key_risks.why_it_matters: The worker acts with VM Contributor on the resource group. A mapping error (display name instead of object id, stale assignment, pooled host) restarts someone else's desktop; an over-scoped identity makes any bug in the worker a tenant-wide outage tool.
required_controls: Resolve the user by Entra object id + tenant id from the validated JWT only
Restart only hosts whose assignment is personal and currently assigned to that object id; refuse pooled hosts explicitly
Scope the managed identity to a custom role with only Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/restart/action on personal host pools, or at minimum per-host-pool resource groups

key_risks.headline: Restart loops and ARM throttling
key_risks.why_it_matters: A compromised or careless user can keep a host rebooting, and bursts of restarts count against ARM subscription throttling limits that NME's autoscale also depends on.
required_controls: Enforce one restart per user per 10 minutes and a per-host-pool concurrency cap in the worker, not in the bot
Require the confirmation card server-side when the admin setting is on
Front the endpoint with request size limits and per-source rate limiting

key_risks.headline: Feature exposed without admin intent
key_risks.why_it_matters: The per-host-pool flag is the gate for the whole feature. If it defaults to on or can be changed by a non-admin, every Teams user in the tenant gains restart capability silently.
required_controls: Default off per host pool; only the NME admin role can change it; write flag changes to the audit log

key_risks.headline: Restarts that cannot be attributed
key_risks.why_it_matters: Admins will investigate 'who rebooted my desktop'. Without actor, host, source (Teams) and correlation id in a tamper-evident log, the feature creates disputes it cannot settle.
required_controls: Audit event with Entra object id, tenant id, VM resource id, result, activity id and UTC time to Log Analytics
Do not persist the free-text message body

design_conditions: Record decisions for all seven §6.3 Architectural Security Review domains (currently missing: TM-ARCH-REVIEW)
Treat every Medium and High threat: plan a mitigation with a work item, accept with a Risk Register entry, transfer, or reject with a reason (TM-TREATED)
Answer the open question on bot registration type; if multi-tenant, add tenant-id validation as a mandatory mitigation
Confirm the managed identity scope and replace Virtual Machine Contributor with a restart-only custom role
Obtain Security Team design approval (Tier 2, TM-APPROVAL)
testing_requirements: Negative tests: JWT with wrong audience, wrong issuer, expired, wrong tenant id are rejected with 401 and logged
Authorization tests: user A cannot restart user B's host; pooled hosts are refused; stale assignment is refused
Rate-limit test: second restart within 10 minutes is refused server-side even if the bot is bypassed
Fuzz the /api/teams/activity payload (ISMS-DEV-003 §8.1.3) including oversized and malformed activities
DAST against the QA deployment with the endpoint enabled
Verify the host-pool flag defaults to off on a fresh install and that only admins can change it
Verify audit events contain actor, host, result and correlation id and that message text is absent
compliance_notes: Entra object id and display name are personal data under GDPR; processing is transient and the audit log is existing NME processing, but the retention period for new audit entries must follow the Logging and Monitoring Policy.
ISO 27001 A.8.27 (secure architecture) and SSDF PW.1/PW.2 are satisfied by completing the Tier 2 review before development starts.
The feature performs a privileged operation in the customer tenant; document the restart-only role in the customer-facing permissions reference.
recommendation_rationale: The design is sound and the exposure is bounded (single tenant, no new persisted data, restart-only operation). Proceed once the design conditions above are met: strict JWT and tenant validation, object-id based host resolution, a restart-only identity scope, server-side rate limiting, and a secure-by-default enable flag, with the Tier 2 review and Security Team approval recorded in the threat model.
